text:
Sean Monahan left Friday's loss in Buffalo with a lower-body injury, and RotoWire reports he expects to play tonight. Columbus needs him back, and it needs the old version of him.

He has one goal in 15 games and none in his last 14, on 3.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances). That's bad luck; he's shooting 6.7% against a normal range of 10 to 14%. The bigger concern is that the Blue Jackets have only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, seven points worse than when he sits.

That's out of character. Evolving-Hockey had him driving offense last season (92nd percentile among forwards), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.1 primary shot assists per 60, 89th percentile. He's 32, past 890 career games, and a playmaker whose value shows up in his teammates' shots. Our projection sees about 37 points. If he's healthy, we'd expect his on-ice numbers to drift back toward even before his goals do.
